name: Whist Minnesota
description: Partnership trick-taking game with no trumps. Each hand players secretly choose to play high (Grand: take 7+ tricks) or low (Nula: take 6 or fewer) by laying a red or black card; first side to reach the target score (typically 13) wins.

overview.description: Partnership trick-taking game with no trumps. Each hand players secretly choose to play high (Grand: take 7+ tricks) or low (Nula: take 6 or fewer) by laying a red or black card; first side to reach the target score (typically 13) wins.

history.origins: Minnesota Whist was brought to the Upper Midwest by Scandinavian and Norwegian immigrants. It is a simplified Whist with no trumps and optional high (Grand) or low (Nula) play each hand.
timeline: 19th–20th century: Brought to Upper Midwest by Norwegian immigrants; simplified from Whist with no trumps.

setup.players: Four players in two fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Rank A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2.
setup.dealing: One card at a time clockwise from left of dealer until each player has 13 cards.

rules.objective: Be the first partnership to reach the agreed target score (typically 13). Each hand is either Grand (take 7+ tricks) or Nula (take 6 or fewer); players secretly choose by laying a red card (pass/low) or black card (grand/high).
rules.gameplay: After the deal, each player lays one card face-down (red = pass, black = grand). If any card is black, the hand is Grand and the goal is to take at least 7 tricks; the player to the right of whoever granded leads. If all four are red (Nula), the goal is to take 6 or fewer tricks; the player to the dealer's left leads. Follow suit; highest card of the led suit wins the trick (no trumps). Winner of each trick leads the next. Scoring: Nula hands score 1 point per trick under 7 for the side that chose low; Grand hands score 1 point per trick over 6 if your side granded, or 2 points per trick over 6 if the opposing side granded.
keyRules: No trumps; highest of led suit wins trick.
Each hand: secret pass (red) or grand (black) choice; all pass = Nula (lose tricks), any grand = Grand (win tricks).
First to target score (typically 13) wins the game.

scoring.description: Nula: 1 point per trick under 7. Grand: 1 point per trick over 6 if your side granded, 2 per trick over 6 if opponents granded. First to target (typically 13) wins.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach the agreed target score (typically 13 points) wins the game.
